newsitem.title: UK: Conrad to buy Sheffield United football club.
newsitem.headline: Conrad to buy Sheffield United football club.

text.p: Diversified British leisurewear company Conrad Plc said on Wednesday that it has agreed upon the terms of a recommended offer for Sheffield United Football Club Ltd.
It said in a statement it planned to raise around 12.5 million stg by way of a placing and open offer, which is conditional upon the acquisition being effected.
The proceeds from the placing will be used to fund the costs associated with the acquisition, to repay debt, provide additional working capital and finance to strengthen the playing staff.
The placing and open offer have been underwritten by Apax Partners & Co Corporate Finance Ltd. HSBC James Capel are brokers to the placing.
Conrad said in October it was in talks with Sheffield Utd.

It said the total value of the consideration payable, based on the price of 60p at which new Conrad shares are being offered, is around 14.9 million stg payable through the issue of up to 24.8 million new Conrad ordinary shares.

Conrad said its ordinary shares would remain suspended until the acquisition was completed or until the offer lapsed. Conrad also plans to change the company's name to Sheffield United Plc and make changes on the board.
The company also wants to consolidate every ten ordinary shares of 1p each in the capital of the Company into one ordinary share of 10p each.
Directors of Sheffield United plus other United shareholders, representing 91.33 percent of the ordinary share capital, have already accepted the offer.
